topics.angle: A developer upgrades to Prisma 7, hits a cryptic '__internal' TypeError, and the actual fix is regenerating the client against Prisma 7's new generator setup, not downgrading.
topics.why: Two separate Stack Overflow threads about Prisma v7 errors (5,942 views and 2,182 views) both tagged node.js/typescript show this is a widespread upgrade pain point right now.

topics.topic: TypeScript deprecating baseUrl ahead of v7
topics.angle: TypeScript's tsconfig 'baseUrl' option is being phased out before TypeScript 7, and the fix is moving path resolution onto 'paths' alone, not patching around the warning.
topics.why: The single highest-viewed candidate in this batch is a Stack Overflow question with 24,499 views asking exactly about this deprecation notice.

topics.angle: Believing 'Next.js 16 just works out of the box' doesn't hold up against three unrelated developer reports of source-map errors, Windows localhost crashes, and broken App Router i18n, all in the same release.
topics.why: Three separate Stack Overflow threads tagged next.js, all about Next.js 16 specifically, with 3,492, 628, and 453 views, point to the same release causing varied real problems.

topics.topic: Agent 'Skills' for Claude Code and Codex
topics.angle: Compare how a 'skill' actually loads and scopes instructions in Claude Code versus Codex, since eight unrelated new repos in under two weeks are all built around this one concept.
topics.why: GitHub trending right now is dominated by skill-related repos (unslop 8,894 stars, ub-mode 7,011, pixelfx 4,867, tstack 3,007, floorplan 2,883, agent-autoloop 2,820, benjitaylor/skills 1,968, teardown 1,967), showing this is the moment's biggest AI-coding-tool trend.

topics.topic: setState inside useEffect isn't as safe as it looks
topics.angle: Calling setState synchronously inside an effect and assuming it fires once cleanly is wrong, since React's own cascading-render behavior can trigger extra render passes.
topics.why: A Stack Overflow question about this exact React warning picked up 4,797 views in roughly a month, tagged reactjs.

topics.topic: CSS filter changing more than the alpha channel
topics.angle: A filter meant to only touch opacity quietly shifts the RGB values too, because CSS filter functions don't operate the way most developers picture color changes working.
topics.why: A Stack Overflow question asking exactly this got 1,075 views, and the behavior matches how MDN documents CSS filter operating on premultiplied color.

topics.topic: Zod's .email() isn't checking what you assume
topics.angle: Developers assume Zod's .email() validates addresses the way a mail server would, but the actual rule is a specific documented pattern that rejects or accepts cases people don't expect.
topics.why: A Stack Overflow question on Zod email validation got 855 views, tagged reactjs, right as Zod-based form validation remains a common setup question.

topics.topic: Should uv.lock be committed to git
topics.angle: Treating Python's uv.lock like a throwaway build artifact and gitignoring it is the wrong default, since uv's own docs call it the reproducibility file you're supposed to commit.
topics.why: A Stack Overflow question asking exactly whether to gitignore uv.lock drew 5,119 views, tagged git, showing real confusion as uv adoption grows.

topics.topic: Conductor, an AI coding agent tool, joining Meta
topics.angle: A standalone AI coding agent orchestration startup just got folded directly into Meta, straight from its own announcement page.
topics.why: The Hacker News post on Conductor's own announcement pulled 158 points and 170 comments, a strong signal for an AI-coding-tool audience.
